body_markdown:
Discover 10 nutrient-rich foods and drinks that support immune health during flu season, including citrus fruits, yogurt, lean proteins, milk, and green tea.


As flu season approaches, maintaining a healthy lifestyle becomes increasingly important. While no single food or drink can prevent influenza or guarantee protection against infections, a balanced diet can provide essential nutrients that help the immune system function properly.


Nutrition experts emphasize the importance of eating a variety of fruits, vegetables, protein-rich foods, and fiber sources to support overall health. Gut health also plays a significant role in immune function, making dietary diversity an important part of a healthy eating routine.


According to nutrition experts featured in a Fox News Digital report published on October 13, 2026, certain foods and beverages can help people meet their nutritional needs during flu season. Here are 10 options to consider adding to your everyday diet.


## 1. Citrus Fruits for Vitamin C


Oranges, lemons, grapefruits, and other citrus fruits are well-known sources of vitamin C, an essential nutrient that supports normal immune function.


Vitamin C helps protect cells from oxidative damage and supports several processes involved in the body's immune response. Other fruits, including kiwis and strawberries, also provide vitamin C and additional beneficial nutrients.


Including a variety of fresh fruit in your daily meals can help you meet your nutritional requirements. Try adding orange slices to breakfast, enjoying kiwi as a snack, or using fresh lemon juice to flavor water and salads.


Although vitamin C is important for health, consuming extra amounts does not guarantee that you will avoid the flu.


## 2. Colorful Vegetables for Essential Nutrients


Eating a variety of colorful vegetables is another practical way to support immune health.


Bell peppers, broccoli, carrots, spinach, and sweet potatoes provide different combinations of vitamins, minerals, antioxidants, and other plant compounds. Red, orange, green, and yellow vegetables each contribute to a varied diet.


Registered dietitian Erin Palinski-Wade recommends including a wide range of colorful produce in everyday meals, according to the Fox News Digital report.


Try adding vegetables to soups, preparing a mixed salad, or roasting broccoli and bell peppers as a side dish. Choosing different colors throughout the week can help broaden the range of nutrients in your diet.


## 3. Yogurt and Kefir for Gut Health


The digestive system and immune system are closely connected. The gut microbiome contains a diverse community of microorganisms that contribute to digestive health and interact with immune processes.


Yogurt containing live cultures and kefir are fermented foods that may help support a healthy gut microbiome. They can also provide protein, calcium, and other nutrients, depending on the product.


Choose plain yogurt when possible and add fresh fruit, nuts, or seeds for extra flavor and nutritional value. Check product labels because not all fermented products contain the same live cultures or offer identical benefits.


Fermented foods can be part of a healthy diet, but they should not be considered a treatment or guaranteed defense against respiratory infections.


## 4. Beans, Nuts, and Seeds for Fiber


Dietary fiber supports digestive health and helps nourish beneficial gut microorganisms. However, many people do not consume the recommended amount of fiber each day.


Beans, lentils, almonds, chia seeds, pumpkin seeds, and other plant foods can help increase daily fiber intake.


Legumes are particularly versatile. Add chickpeas to salads, prepare lentil soup, or serve beans with whole grains for a satisfying meal. Nuts and seeds can also be sprinkled over oatmeal, yogurt, or vegetable dishes.


Increase fiber gradually and drink enough water to help your digestive system adjust comfortably.


## 5. Lean Meat and Eggs for Protein


Protein is essential for building and maintaining tissues, and it contributes to the production of immune cells and other substances involved in normal immune function.


Chicken, turkey, eggs, fish, tofu, and legumes are useful sources of protein. Including different protein sources in your meals can help you obtain a range of essential nutrients.


For example, eggs can provide a convenient breakfast option, while grilled chicken or tofu can form the basis of a balanced lunch. Pairing protein with vegetables and whole grains creates a meal that supports overall nutritional needs.


Eating adequate protein is especially important when your body needs to maintain and repair tissues.


## 6. Pumpkin Seeds and Chickpeas for Zinc


Zinc is an essential mineral that supports normal immune function and many other processes in the body.


Pumpkin seeds, chickpeas, beans, seafood, meat, and dairy products can contribute to zinc intake. Eggs also provide protein and several other nutrients.


Try adding pumpkin seeds to salads or oatmeal, or use chickpeas in homemade hummus and grain bowls.


The key is to obtain enough zinc through a balanced diet rather than assuming that larger quantities will provide greater protection. Excessive zinc supplementation can cause side effects and interfere with the absorption of other minerals.


## 7. Milk for Vitamins and Minerals


Milk provides several nutrients involved in maintaining general health, including protein, calcium, and vitamin B12. Depending on the product and whether it is fortified, it may also supply vitamins A and D.


Registered dietitian Lauren Manaker highlighted milk as a potentially useful beverage for meeting nutritional needs during flu season in the report.


Some people avoid dairy when they have a cold because they believe it increases mucus production. However, the Mayo Clinic notes that there is little scientific evidence that milk causes increased mucus production.


Milk may create a temporary coating sensation in the mouth or throat, which some people interpret as extra mucus.


If you are lactose intolerant, lactose-free dairy milk can provide many of the same nutrients as regular milk. Fortified alternatives may also be suitable, although their protein and nutrient content varies by product.


## 8. Water for Hydration


Staying hydrated is important throughout the year, particularly when you are unwell.


Water supports normal bodily functions and helps maintain moisture in the mouth and airways. Adequate fluid intake can also help replace fluids lost through sweating or fever.


Keep water readily available throughout the day and drink regularly. Individual fluid needs vary according to activity, temperature, health status, and other factors.


People who have been advised to restrict fluids because of a medical condition should follow their healthcare professional's guidance.


## 9. Green Tea for Antioxidants


Green tea contains plant compounds called polyphenols, including catechins, that have been studied for their antioxidant properties.


Enjoying unsweetened green tea can be a convenient way to add variety to your daily fluid intake. It also contains caffeine, so people who are sensitive to caffeine may prefer smaller servings or caffeine-free alternatives.


Although green tea can contribute to a healthy lifestyle, evidence does not establish that drinking it prevents influenza. It is best viewed as one beverage option within a balanced diet.


## 10. Ginger Tea and Broth for Comfort and Fluids


Warm drinks such as ginger tea and broth can make it easier to maintain fluid intake, especially when you have a sore throat or reduced appetite.


Broth may also provide sodium and other nutrients, depending on the ingredients. Choosing lower-sodium options can be helpful for people who need to monitor their salt intake.


Ginger tea offers a warming alternative to plain water, although claims that it prevents or cures the flu should be treated cautiously.


These drinks can provide comfort during illness, but they do not replace appropriate medical care when symptoms are severe or persistent.


## Other Habits That Support Immune Health


Food is only one part of maintaining a healthy immune system. Several everyday habits also contribute to overall well-being:


- **Get sufficient sleep:** Consistent, restorative sleep supports normal immune function.
- **Manage stress:** Relaxation techniques, social connection, and regular breaks can help manage ongoing stress.
- **Stay physically active:** Regular movement supports general health and can improve sleep and well-being.
- **Follow recommended vaccinations:** Seasonal influenza vaccination is an important measure for reducing the risk of flu and its complications.
- **Practice good hygiene:** Wash your hands regularly, improve indoor ventilation, and follow public health advice to help reduce the spread of respiratory infections.


## Conclusion


Supporting your immune system during flu season starts with consistent, healthy habits. Citrus fruits, colorful vegetables, fermented foods, fiber-rich legumes, protein sources, and zinc-containing foods can all contribute valuable nutrients to a balanced diet.


Water, green tea, milk, ginger tea, and broth can also help you maintain hydration according to your individual needs.


Remember that no specific food, drink, or supplement can guarantee immunity against the flu. Focus on dietary variety, adequate sleep, physical activity, vaccination, and appropriate healthcare to support your health throughout the season.

## Medical Disclaimer


This article is intended for general informational and educational purposes only. It is not a substitute for professional medical advice, diagnosis, or treatment. Foods and beverages discussed here may support normal immune function but cannot guarantee prevention or treatment of influenza or other illnesses. Consult a qualified healthcare professional before starting supplements, making significant dietary changes, or treating persistent or severe symptoms. Follow current public health recommendations regarding influenza vaccination and infection prevention.
